questions.q: "Philippine ebony" refers to:
questions.n: Kamagong (Diospyros) is the native ebony.

questions.q: Inside corners of baseboards and crown molding are best fitted with a:
questions.n: Coping profiles one piece to the face of the other and doesn't open up.

questions.q: Weakest of these wood joints:
questions.n: A simple lap has little interlock and relies on fasteners.

questions.q: Drying lumber in a chamber with controlled heat, humidity and air flow is:
questions.n: Kilns dry fast without defects.

questions.q: The roof of Mactan-Cebu International Airport Terminal 2 is framed in:
questions.n: Its signature arches are glulam.

questions.q: Picture frames, casings and moldings are typically joined with a:
questions.n: 45° miters hide end grain at corners.

questions.q: Lumber for construction framing should be dried to a moisture content of about:
questions.n: 19% is the "dry lumber" threshold.

questions.q: Narra's grain is best described as:
questions.n: Its interlocked figure gives narra its prized pattern.

questions.q: Moderately hard, light, mahogany-like in grain, fine indoors but not durable in ground contact. This describes:
questions.n: Tanguile is the classic interior "Philippine mahogany."

questions.q: Which joint is commonly made with screws alone, no glue needed?
questions.n: Pocket screws clamp and hold by themselves.

questions.q: The box structure of a cabinet that holds the doors and drawers is the:
questions.n: The carcass (case) is the cabinet body.

questions.q: Machined, ready-made interlocking edges common on flooring are:
questions.n: T&G boards lock together.

questions.q: Which native timber is used for heavy, durable work like saltwater piles and bridges?
questions.n: Aranga is a very durable structural hardwood suited to marine use.

questions.q: Thin veneers glued with grain crossing at right angles make:
questions.n: Cross-graining gives plywood its stability.

questions.q: Which of these wood defects grows in the tree rather than appearing during drying?
questions.n: Knots are branch bases; the others are seasoning defects.

questions.q: The trade of fitting and joining wood components, such as cabinetry and joints, is:
questions.n: Joinery is fine wood joint work.

questions.q: Wood baseboards are fixed with:
questions.n: Small heads can be set and filled.

questions.q: Which joint is basically a concealed, angled toe-nail done with screws?
questions.n: Pocket screws enter at an angle like toe-nailing.

questions.q: The strongest, most rigid of these classic wood joints:
questions.n: The tenon locks into the mortise on several faces.

questions.q: Lauan is traded in two varieties:
questions.n: Red lauan and white lauan.

questions.q: A jack rafter is to a roof what a ______ is to a stud wall.
questions.n: Both are shortened members cut off by an opening or hip.

questions.q: Which timber failure comes from load, not drying?
questions.n: Crushing is compression failure under load.

questions.q: Which material is made mostly of organic cellulose fibers?
questions.n: Wood is a cellulose-and-lignin composite.

questions.q: Compared with plywood of the same thickness, plyboard is:
questions.n: The solid strip core resists bending.

questions.q: T&G wood flooring over a concrete slab is laid on:
questions.n: Sleepers create a nailing base and an air gap.

questions.q: Called Philippine red mahogany, it takes stain well and is common in furniture and cabinets:
questions.n: Red lauan is the darker lauan.

questions.q: Thin veneers laminated parallel into beam and header stock, not cabinetry, make:
questions.n: LVL is a structural composite.

questions.q: Which of these is sold as Philippine mahogany?
questions.n: Tanguile and lauan are the "Philippine mahogany" timbers.

questions.q: Which is a biological hazard, not a seasoning defect?
questions.n: Insects and fungi are biological.

questions.q: A weak, light board of bonded wood chips, often veneered or painted and confused with OSB, is:
questions.n: Particle board uses small chips; OSB uses large oriented strands.

questions.q: Phenolic resin and cellulose sheets pressed under heat and high pressure give:
questions.n: Very hard, moisture-resistant panels.

questions.q: Cabinet doors set flush inside the face frame openings are:
questions.n: Inset doors sit within the frame, not over it.

questions.q: Yellow-to-red, weather- and termite-resistant, prized and now threatened, and the national tree. Which wood?
questions.n: Narra (Pterocarpus indicus) is the national tree, valued for color and durability.

questions.q: Uneven drying that twists, bows or cups lumber is called:
questions.n: Warp covers all those distortions.

questions.q: For shelving, which board is usually chosen for stiffness?
questions.n: The solid core resists sagging.

questions.q: A core of solid wood strips sandwiched between veneers is:
questions.n: Blockboard or plyboard has a strip core, which also makes it stiffer than plywood.

questions.q: Bamboo floor planks are most commonly installed:
questions.n: Click-lock floating installation is the norm.

questions.q: Cross-bracing between members to stop them twisting is most associated with:
questions.n: Joist bridging spreads load and prevents rotation.

questions.q: When common wire nails might split the wood, switch to:
questions.n: Box nails have thinner shanks.

questions.q: Smooth, machinable and uniform, used for furniture, cabinets and speaker boxes:
questions.n: Medium-density fiberboard machines cleanly.

questions.q: Coco lumber is least suited for:
questions.n: It's hard to machine to fine profiles and moves with humidity.

questions.q: Which wood problem comes from long exposure to moisture rather than from drying?
questions.n: Fungal decay needs sustained moisture.

questions.q: For a strong T&G joint, the tongue is about ______ of the board thickness.
questions.n: A third leaves enough wood on each side of the groove.

questions.q: In Western wood-frame houses, the dominant framing method builds each floor as a deck for the next storey. This is:
questions.n: Platform framing replaced balloon framing.

questions.q: OSB or plywood skins over a foam core, used to frame houses:
questions.n: SIPs are wood-skinned.

questions.q: An Ortigas condo will sit unoccupied and unair-conditioned for weeks at a time. Which wood-look floor stays flattest through humidity swings?
questions.n: Cross-laminated plies resist the cupping and gapping of solid wood.

questions.q: Biscuit joints are mostly used to:
o: Align and join boards edge to edge
questions.n: Oval biscuits align panels being glued up.

questions.q: The joint that signals fine craftsmanship and resists pulling apart, as in drawer fronts, is the:
questions.n: Interlocking tails and pins resist withdrawal.

questions.q: A common, economical wood for door jambs is:
questions.n: Tanguile machines well and costs less than the hardwoods.

questions.q: Kamagong is prized for its:
questions.n: Philippine ebony is dark, very dense and now endangered.
